notes: LA is a two-body lobbying-disclosure regime split across two titles in the Revised Statutes: Title 24 (Legislature and Laws) houses the Legislative Lobbyist Disclosure Act at La. R.S. 24:50-58.1, and Title 49 (State Administration) houses the Executive Branch Lobbying Disclosure Act at La. R.S. 49:71-78.1. Pass-1 selected ONLY 'revised-statutes/' from the LA top-level Justia index because LA's top level lists codes (not titles) and BOTH lobbying titles live under Revised Statutes. The Civil Code was correctly skipped at pass-1 - it is private law (persons, things, obligations) and contains no lobbying provisions; the other code-level entries (Children's Code, Code of Civil Procedure, Code of Criminal Procedure, Code of Evidence) are likewise unrelated. Pass-2 cascaded three times: (1) revised-statutes/ -> selected title-24/ and title-49/; (2) title-24/ -> selected the 13 per-section URLs for sections 24:50-58.1 (intervening section 24:59 is repealed; sections 24:61-63 belong to the Emergency Interim Legislative Succession Act and are intentionally excluded); (3) title-49/ -> selected the 9 per-section URLs for sections 49:71-78.1 (the regime prior's '49:71 through 49:83' range is approximate - in the 2025 codification, 49:79-83 do not exist as separate sections; the act has been consolidated into 49:71-78.1). LA uses a flat per-section URL convention (rs-<title>-<section>/) within each title; there is no intermediate chapter slug in URLs, so the section URLs returned at pass-2 cascade are themselves the statute-text leaves. Pass-3 was not invoked because per-section URLs are leaves by convention (analogous to Wisconsin's per-section-leaf pattern, Example D in pass-2 prompt). 22 proposed URLs total: 13 from Title 24 + 9 from Title 49. tree_depth=4 (state -> code -> title -> section), excluding the vintage segment per TX 2015 convention.
